\section[criticar]{criticar — to criticise}

\label{lesson:ES-C579-criticar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for in favour, then the Spanish for opposed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: criticar}
\textbf{criticar} — \textquotedblleft{}to criticise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No me gusta criticar a la gente.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I do not like criticising people.}
\end{quote}

Spelling: \emph{critiqué} in the past, \emph{critique} in the subjunctive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{criticar} is built on \emph{crítico}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{criticus} and Greek \emph{kritikos} 'able to judge', from \emph{krinein} 'to separate, to decide' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{criticar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{criticar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{criticar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for in favour, then the Spanish for opposed, then say \emph{criticar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does criticar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To criticise\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la crítica]{la crítica — the criticism; the review}

\label{lesson:ES-C579-critica}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for opposed, then the Spanish for to criticise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la crítica}
\textbf{la crítica} — \textquotedblleft{}the criticism; the review\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Acepto la crítica con calma.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I accept the criticism calmly.}
\end{quote}

Also a review of a book or film: \emph{la crítica de la película}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{la crítica} is built on \emph{crítico}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{criticus}, taken from Greek \emph{kritikos} 'able to judge', from \emph{krinein} 'to judge' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la crítica}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for opposed, then the Spanish for to criticise, then say \emph{la crítica} again
\end{itemize}

\section[contradecir]{contradecir — to contradict}

\label{lesson:ES-C579-contradecir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to criticise, then the Spanish for the criticism.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: contradecir}
\textbf{contradecir} — \textquotedblleft{}to contradict\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No me gusta contradecir a mi jefe.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I do not like contradicting my boss.}
\end{quote}

Like \emph{decir}: \emph{contradigo, contradije, contradicho}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{contradecir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{contradicere} 'to speak against', built from \emph{contra} and \emph{dicere} 'to say', and rebuilt on \emph{decir} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{contradecir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{contradecir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{contradecir}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to criticise, then the Spanish for the criticism, then say \emph{contradecir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does contradecir mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To contradict\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[reconocer]{reconocer — to admit; to recognise}

\label{lesson:ES-C579-reconocer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the criticism, then the Spanish for to contradict.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: reconocer}
\textbf{reconocer} — \textquotedblleft{}to admit; to recognise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Reconozco que me equivoqué.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I admit that I was wrong.}
\end{quote}

Like \emph{conocer}: \emph{reconozco}. In a debate it means to admit a point.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{reconocer} is inherited from Latin \emph{recognoscere} 'to know again, to examine', built on \emph{cognoscere} 'to get to know', the same verb as \emph{conocer} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reconocer}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reconocer}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{reconocer}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the criticism, then the Spanish for to contradict, then say \emph{reconocer} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does reconocer mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To admit; to recognise\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[absurdo]{absurdo — absurd, ridiculous}

\label{lesson:ES-C579-absurdo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to contradict, then the Spanish for to admit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: absurdo}
\textbf{absurdo} — \textquotedblleft{}absurd, ridiculous\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Es absurdo pagar tanto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is absurd to pay so much.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Es absurdo que} + subjunctive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{absurdo} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{absurdus} 'out of tune, senseless', built from \emph{ab} and \emph{surdus} 'deaf, dull-sounding' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{absurdo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{absurdo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{absurdo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to contradict, then the Spanish for to admit, then say \emph{absurdo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
